note: A mouse model of TUBA4A spastic ataxia (SPAX11) exhibits overt ataxia and Purkinje neuron degeneration, supporting Purkinje cell loss as a primary driver of cerebellar pathology.

evidence.text: In a CRISPR-engineered mouse model harboring a dominant Tuba4a mutation (Q176P) modeling SPAX11, mice develop overt ataxia and Purkinje neuron degeneration by 30 days of age.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: However, by 30 days these mice have overt ataxia, Purkinje neuron degeneration, and extensive skeletal muscle defects, which contribute to a decreased lifespan. Dominant TUBA4A mutations in humans are associated with spastic ataxia type 11 (SPAX11), congenital myopathy type 26 (CMYO26), and frontotemporal dementia/amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 9 (FTDALS9).
